label: 90W 802.3bt Type 4 managed PoE midspan
description: SNMP-managed single-port midspan delivering the full 90 W of 802.3bt Type 4 at 56 V/1.6 A over four pairs into a gigabit link, for high-power APs, laptops over PoE and 4K PTZ cameras. It negotiates class 8 power and reports per-port consumption, so the 90 W is only committed after the PD is classified.

poe.note: The sheet is headed "90W Single Port Multi-Gig Power over Ethernet", and its model table carries the N6 part in the same column set: "POE90U-1BT-N6-R 1G 56V >10mA 1.6A 54-57V" (read 2026-11-21). The product page prints "Output Power - 90W, Output Current - 1.6A, Power/Port - 90" (https://www.phihong.com/products/power-over-ethernet/poe90u-1bt-n6-r/). One port, so the device total is the port ceiling.

notes: STANDARD CLAIM, corrected 2026-11-20. The vendor page heads the product "POE Injector 90W Midspan with SNMP - IEEE802.3bt - 1G" with "Output Power - 90W, Output Volt - 56V, Output Current - 1.6A, Power/Port - 90" and "IEEE802.3bt Compliant" (https://www.phihong.com/products/power-over-ethernet/poe90u-1bt-n6-r/, read 2026-11-20); the POE90U-1BT-X data sheet repeats "IEEE802.3bt Compliant" and "Total Output Power 90W" (https://www.phihong.com/wp-content/uploads/POE90U-1BT-X-R.pdf, read 2026-11-20). Only 802.3bt is declared because that is the only standard the sheet names - the same shape as devices/moxa/eds-g4012-8p-4qgs-lvb-t.json, which declares bt alone; the 60 W sibling's sheet names af/at/bt explicitly and so does that entry. It declared no standard at all beside a 90 W port, which is 802.3bt Type 4 (90 W at the PSE, Cisco Catalyst 9000 PoE Configuration Guide, Table 1: https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/switches/lan/c9000/infra/poe/poe-configuration-guide/g-poe/c-poe.html). The file contradicted itself before this: its `role` already read "802.3bt-type-4". test/poe-injector-standard.test.js holds the rule.
